title: LLM-driven Multi-agent Collaboration
use_cases: Implement when coordinating local narrative modifications with global story consistency

content:
Recent work shows that collaborative LLM agents exhibit superior cognitive and reasoning capabilities over individual LLMs in complex tasks, and multi-agent collaboration has been widely applied to content creation (Zhang et al. 2024b; Durante et al. 2024; Guo et al. 2024; Xi et al. 2025; Qian et al. 2025). CAMEL (Li et al. 2023) proposes a communicative agent framework to study collaborative behaviors and multi-agent interactions. ChatDev (Qian et al. 2024) creates virtual companies where agents play professional roles to solve complex tasks through collaboration. AutoAgents (Chen et al. 2024a) develops an automatic agent generation framework to dynamically create and coordinate specialized agents based on task requirements. STORM (Shao et al. 2024) introduces a multi-agent writing system that synthesizes topic outlines through retrieval and multi-perspective question asking to generate long-form articles. Agents’ Room (Huot et al. 2025) consider story generation as a multi-step collaboration problem, proposing planning and writing agents to achieve enhanced story coherence. Chain of Agents (Zhang et al. 2024a) addresses long-context processing challenges by distributing tasks across multiple LLM agents in a sequential chain for improved efficiency and accuracy. Du et al. (Du et al. 2023) show that multi-agent debate mechanisms enhance factuality and reasoning capabilities in language models through collaborative deliberation processes. A multi-agent framework (Du et al. 2023) enhances factuality and reasoning in language models via collaborative deliberation. Debate-to-Write (Hu et al. 2025) introduces persona-driven multi-agent frameworks for diverse argument generation, enabling more comprehensive perspective coverage. AgentCoord (Pan et al. 2024) provides visual exploration tools for understanding and optimizing coordination strategies in LLM-based multi-agent systems.

Existing work primarily adopts role-playing and collaboration to simplify complex tasks; however, in our task, it remains challenging to coordinate local modifications with the global narrative. We leverage the logical reasoning power of multi-agent LLMs to implement divide-and-conquer strategies along both task and feature dimensions, enabling coordinated revisions across multiple granularities and locations.

#### Dataset

To facilitate a comprehensive and balanced evaluation, we constructed a dataset of 50 narrative scripts across five genres, evenly sourced from five representative works, with a mix of human-written and AI-generated scripts. The dataset is constructed from the following work:

•

Writingprompts (Fan, Lewis, and Dauphin 2018): A collection of creative stories from the Reddit community.

•

Dramatron (Mirowski et al. 2023): High-quality generated scripts using a hierarchical generation strategy.

•

DOC (Yang et al. 2023): Long stories generated using a two-stage outline control strategy.

•

MoPS (Ma, Qiao, and Liu 2024): Generated scripts leveraging Well-crafted modular premise synthesis.

•

Agents’ Room (Huot et al. 2025): High-quality stories collected through collaborative writing.

The detailed statistics of the experimental datasets are provided in Appendix F.
